question: On the publishing side of this project's apt channel: where do packages get published to, how many old versions are kept, what identity does the repository advertise in its release metadata, and where in the tree does the distribution index live? Cite path:line for each.
answer:
The project publishes its apt channel to the GitHub repository identified by
`REPO_SLUG` — `namastex888/fde-station-apt` (channel/publish.sh:52).  Two old
versions are retained, set via `KEEP="${KEEP:-2}"` (channel/publish.sh:56). The
repository's release metadata advertises `ORIGIN="FDE Station"` (line 59), `SUITE="stable"`
(line 61), and `CODENAME="stable"` (line 62). The distribution index lives at
`dists/stable/InRelease` (line 257, written as `"$DIST_DIR/InRelease"`) and
`dists/stable/Release` (line 226, `rel="$DIST_DIR/Release"`). The packages index
is written to `dists/stable/main/binary-amd64/Packages` (line 221,
`mv "$NEW_PKGS" "$IDX_DIR/Packages"`), where `DIST_DIR` is defined as
`dists/$SUITE` (line 175) and `IDX_DIR` as `$DIST_DIR/$COMPONENT/binary-$ARCH`
(line 176), with `COMPONENT="main"` (line 63) and `ARCH="amd64"` (line 64).
